en: The Avadāna of the Gift of Earth (Pāṃśupradāna-avadāna),
...it happens.
Having heard that, Gupta the perfumer thought: "Noble sirs, while I am still living in the household life... [GBM 1508.2] ...it will happen.
"We shall give that person as an attendant-monk (*paścācchramaṇa*) to the Noble One. The Elder said,
"My child, it is indeed so."
...he enjoyed himself with her until she became pregnant;
when nine months were completed, she gave birth.
[He was] handsome.

After performing his birth festival in detail, he was given the name Aśvagupta. He was raised with a nurse. When he had grown up, he was entrusted to a teacher for training in appropriate crafts. Then, the Elder Śāṇavāsa...
“...he will be your son; we shall give him to you as an attendant-monk (*paścācchramaṇa*). This son has been born to you.
“...what need have I for a single son? Whatever other second son we may have, we shall give him to you as an attendant-monk.”
He did not see it.
Then the Elder said, "So be it. When his second son was born, he became [a certain state].
At that time, the Elder Śāṇavāsī approached the perfumer Gupta and said, "It was promised by you..."

“I shall give it. And this second son of yours has been born; grant permission, for I shall cause him to go forth. Gupto said: “He who shall protect the household, but as for our third son—he, O Noble One, shall be Upagupta. He saw that he was not.
He replied, "So be it. Then,
as for Gupta’s third son—
[he had] a head shaped like a parasol, a broad forehead, and had surpassed human appearance without yet having attained [divine] form.
...reared on milk, curd, butter, honey, and other such things; and from the very day he was born, [he began to grow].
From that time forward, he began to flourish with various kinds of seeds, such as [grains and so forth]. His birth [story] is related in detail.
He was introduced to the calculation of numbers and seals, and before long he became a master of them. Then, [he became] a reciter of the Gāndhārī...
...he obtained [it],
until the Elder Śāṇavāsī, having approached Guptaka, said:
"Noble one..."
"I shall give this for the sake of a junior monk; furthermore, this third son has been born to you.
If there is no interruption in your income, then I will grant permission."
And when he had made that appointment,
[the rain of the True Dharma] arose; having refreshed many people with the sprays of the True Dharma, he transcended all fears.
"He has gone forth; alas, he will empty the entire realm! What now is the appropriate time for this?

He will go forth even sooner than that. Then, in order to fulfill his agreement, Māra caused all the people throughout the entire region to take up material goods and receive great profit on that account, until—
The Elder Śāṇavāsika was standing there selling perfumes. Then the Elder Śāṇavāsika said: "Child, what..."
“Thus,” he said, “Elder, I do not know whether they are afflicted or unafflicted, nor whether they are mental factors. [He replied: “They are dharmas that have not yet arisen.”
"Those that arise together with a defiled mind are defiled. Having grasped this, he said:
"Child, what are they like?"
Those mental states and mental factors proceed; are they defiled? Or...
"My son, if you are able to fully understand the mind and rely upon its antidote, by that means its dark [aspect]..."
"...you set up a black band;
then, when it is not defiled, you set up a white band."
"...let it be so. As long as he has exerted himself, undefiled mental states and mental factors arise in him. He...
...he sets aside one for the white ones, he sets aside one for the black ones, and so on until he sets aside a strip of cloth. And he conducts his business according to the law in Mathurā,
O Vāsava.
[She was] intoxicated with pride.
Her maidservant used to buy perfumes from Upagupta day after day. "Daughter, the perfumer is being robbed! [he said].

“You are bringing many perfumes,” she said. The girl replied: “...and he acts in accordance with the Dharma. Having heard this from Vāsavadattā regarding Upagupta, she was sent toward the east, saying: “I will come into your presence; I desire to experience pleasure together with you.”
...Savadattā was entertained with five hundred *purāṇas*. The thought occurred to her:
"My maidservant has been sent away; my noble son, I have no [need] from you..."
“[There is] a certain purpose... and furthermore: ‘Sister, it is not the time for you to see me,’ until another son of a guild-president [arrived at] his dwelling...”
Having taken five hundred horses for sale, he arrived at Mathurā. He said:
"Taking this [gift] and many presents, [go] to Vāsavadattā."
Having departed from there, he was seized by Vāsavadattā through her supernatural power;
and this horse-dealer was seized along with five hundred [puruṣas].

He took many hundreds of northern goods as a gift and, having gone there, thought: "Whatever pleasure I shall experience with her will result in a loss of this wealth; how can I manage it now? Having given him a dangerous amount of liquor to drink, he had him killed, then threw him into a cesspool, and the horse-dealer entered.

The circle of his kinsmen and relatives, not seeing him anywhere, began to search for him, but they did not find him. Then he was reported by someone to his parents: "He has entered the house of Vāsavadattā.
Thereupon, a great commotion arose in Mathurā. The king heard of it and said: "Go, sirs!"
Then Vāsavadattā,
being abandoned by her kinsmen and not mourned by neutral people,
was seen by the one who perceives the truth: "You have not spoken anything unpleasant here."
But she was granted only pleasant things; through this means,
she was led toward that which yields the fruit of nirvāṇa.
In brief, whatever offense you have committed here against the Sage with a mind blinded by delusion— [all that]... [he],
being thrilled, [spoke].
Sarvāṅga said:
"It was only right that I previously wearied him in many ways;
for by that means, he was treated like a son by his father with conciliation, as if for some offense."
Out of serene faith in the True Dharma, he spoke these words:
"Today you have bestowed upon me a supreme favor, in that you have instilled in me reverence for the Buddha. And this [necklace]...
“...I shall release you on one condition,” he said. Māra asked, “Tell me, what is the condition? The Elder said, “...I shall establish it. “What else do you command? the Elder said.
This, then, is the work of the teaching.
[He spoke these words:
"Be gracious, Elder; what do you command? The Elder replied:
"You go by yourself just as I do for many years;
[he] was not seen."

The physical body of that Lord of the Three Worlds, which resembles a mountain of gold, has not been seen by me. Therefore, O sinless one, grant me this favor. "I have a curiosity regarding the form of the One Possessing the Ten Powers. Māra said: "In that case, listen to my condition as well; it must be fulfilled."

Out of reverence for my teacher, the Omniscient One, and with a mind tender with the recollection of the Buddha, you have now performed worship toward me. What power do I have to endure this act of prostration, which is honored by those free from passion? It is as if I were bearing the placing of a hand upon me. "I shall not consent to it," Māra said. "Therefore, wait for a moment until I have entered the forest."
...due to the power of my intellect, that which was done by me— having fashioned that very form which delights the eyes—
GBM 1515.7 ... then the Elder, having said "So be it," [did so].
Having removed the corpse, he was eager to behold the form of the Tathāgata;

with his garments well-arranged, he began to emerge from that dense forest. For it will be said: "Like one unveiling a highly precious, variegated cloth depicting the Tathāgata, he adorned that forest."
Then,
having manifested the forms of the Elder Śāriputra on his right side and the Elder Mahāmaudgalyāyana on his left side,
as well as the forms of the great śrāvakas beginning with Aniruddha and Subhūti, [he stood] three and a half fathoms in height...
Having shown [him] this, he approached the presence of the Elder Upagupta. And as soon as he saw the Elder Upagupta, he was filled with joy; quickly rising from his seat and gazing [at him], he said:
"Fie on that pitiless woman!
Having encountered impermanence, he has met his destruction. With mindfulness directed toward the Buddha, he remained thus absorbed.
[Then] he, having placed his hands together in *añjali* before Padmamuṣṭi, said: "Oh, how beautiful is the Blessed One’s form! What more need be said?"
He surpassed a forest thick with flowers by his pleasantness, the moon of perfected radiance by his beauty,
the great ocean by his majesty, and Mount Meru by his steadfastness— [he surpassed] the sun.
[He], his heart filled with even greater joy, spoke with a resonant voice: "Aha!

By chance, that stainless form has been manifested, which was produced through hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons by means of speech, body, and mind; having seen which, [the enemy]..."
...he would even be greatly delighted; how much more so,
having forgotten the perception of Māra and established the perception of the Buddha, [would he not be so] at the root...
"Like a tree being cut down, [it pierces] my entire body.
"Venerable sir, venerable sir, you ought not to let the appointed time pass. The Elder said: "What is the appointed time?"
Then the Elder Upagupta, rising from the surface of the earth with a voice faltering with emotion, said:
"O Evil One, it was not out of fear that I bowed to that seer;
rather, having seen his form so lovely to behold, I bowed to that seer, but I did not bow to you."
“...do you pay homage? The Elder said: “Listen to how it is that you have not been honored by me.”
